solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Starter that's Spain to a T, somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of the words before it end up in some unstated new order

explanation.surface: A dish is said to be perfectly Spanish, though nobody can say quite why.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator works on the nine letters of SPAIN TO A T. 'Starter' looks like it means something that begins, but here it is the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian plate of cold meats and olives served before the main meal is a classic first course.

clue.text: Old Greek goat tickling nurses

indicators.note: nurses means holds or cradles, so the words goat tickling contain the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Nurses take to tickling a goat, odd behaviour on any ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like the people doing the tickling, but it is the verb telling you the letters sit inside 'goat tickling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic is the dialect and culture of ancient Athens, so the word can describe an old Greek of that region.

clue.text: Clear running water outside flowed by spring

indicators.note: outside means the river's name goes around the other pieces

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
flowed means ran
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Something clear is described as flowing water fed by a spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running water' looks like a description, but it names a river that flows through the English Midlands; 'outside' wraps it round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass or water you can see straight through is clear, which is the plain sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Country fan's simplistic rubbish drawing one in

parts.note: a pat answer is a glib, simplistic one

indicators.note: drawing ... in means taking something inside, so the word for rubbish wraps round the numeral
completes the phrase drawing in, which signals the containment

parts.note: rot means rubbish or nonsense
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A devotee of some country's facile scribble draws someone into the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country fan' could be a music lover; it means a lover of his country. 'drawing ... in' puts I inside ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loves and supports their homeland is a devoted admirer of that nation.

clue.text: Big glass boat

definitions.meaning: a large drinking glass, for sherry in Britain or beer in Australia
a sailing ship with fore-and-aft rigging on two or more masts

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the word means a large sherry glass, and in Australia a beer glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a tall drinking vessel and a sailing vessel with several masts.

clue.text: Loads of drawings daughter chucked out

indicators.note: chucked out means the letter for daughter is thrown away from the word

parts.note: doodles are idle drawings

explanation.surface: A daughter's huge pile of drawings is thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loads of' looks like one phrase, but 'Loads' is the definition and 'of drawings' gives DOODLES; 'chucked out' drops D.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots or heaps of something, an informal way of saying a great quantity.

clue.text: Name of commoner quietly erased by church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: erased means the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a pleb is a commoner
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A commoner's name is quietly struck off the church register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erased' removes P from PLEB, leaving LEB.
explanation.definitionFit: A big name is a famous person, a star.

clue.text: Gamble large choir will sing here

parts.note: to take a chance is to gamble
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A choir bets big on its next performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a church near the altar holds the stalls where the clergy and choristers sit.

clue.text: Bit of lamb maybe setter served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: gel sets hair, so it is a setter

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler serves a cut of lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the compiler, but it is hair gel. 'served up' turns GEL to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint cut from the hind limb is a common roast cut from a young sheep.

clue.text: Item of clothing I put down in restaurant

indicators.note: in a down entry, put down means the letter I is lowered to a later position

parts.note: a brassiere is a bra, an item of underwear

explanation.surface: Someone sets a garment down in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' moves the I of BRASSIERE two places lower in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-style eating house serving simple dishes and drinks is a kind of informal eatery.

clue.text: The Speaker's dogged disquisition?

indicators.note: what the speaker says is heard, so the word is said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or track them

explanation.surface: The Speaker of the House gives a persistent, long-winded lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dogged' looks like 'persistent', but it is the verb meaning followed: TRACKED.
explanation.definitionFit: A pamphlet or treatise arguing a case is a written discourse, so it fits a formal essay.

clue.text: Called into London park with a climber

indicators.note: into means the word for called goes inside the park's name

parts.note: Hyde Park is a large park in central London
rang means telephoned or called

explanation.surface: Someone phoned into a London park with a mountaineer in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' looks like a mountaineer; it is a climbing plant. HYDE Park is in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: One species is a climbing shrub that grows up walls, so it counts as a climbing plant.

clue.text: Die, as one might in a casino?

definitions.text: Die, as one might in a casino?

parts.words: Die, as one might in a casino?
parts.note: the idiom for dying literally means exchanging gaming tokens for money when leaving a casino

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a slang way of saying die; at a casino it literally describes a gambler turning tokens back into money.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for death taken from gambling, where players settle up at the end of play.

clue.text: Meet painter, horribly self-indulgent

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters of the words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Meeting an artist turns out to be a ghastly, indulgent affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges the letters of MEET PAINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking restraint, especially with drink, is the core of being given to excess and self-indulgent.

clue.text: Spooked, began to bury first of loot

indicators.note: to bury means the word for began covers over the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: started means began

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A thief, frightened, sets about hiding the start of the haul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bury' puts L, the first letter of 'loot', inside STARTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightened suddenly, as a horse is when it shies, is what a spooked creature feels.

clue.text: Lapps tear apart this fruit

indicators.note: tearing something apart breaks it up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arctic herders rip a piece of fruit to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart' with 'tear' rearranges LAPPS TEAR; 'tear' is part of the fodder, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical tree bears a round purple fruit whose cut cross-section shows a star shape.

clue.text: One criticising alternative to Thatcher?

definitions.meaning: to slate is to criticise harshly, so this is someone who does that
a roofer who uses slates rather than straw, with a nod to the prime minister Margaret Thatcher

explanation.walkthrough: 'Thatcher' looks like Margaret Thatcher, the British prime minister, but it is a roofer working with straw; this tradesman roofs with slates instead.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for both a harsh critic and a tradesman who covers roofs with slate tiles.

clue.text: Case that would be haunting under English

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under the letter for English means that letter sits on top, so removing it leaves this word

parts.note: something haunting stirs memories, so it is evocative

explanation.surface: A detective's case would turn into a ghost story beneath English skies.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer with E placed over it, in the down entry, would make EVOCATIVE, meaning haunting.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the form of a noun used when addressing someone is one of the cases.

clue.text: Content to be a flirt?

parts.note: a tease is someone who flirts provocatively

explanation.surface: Is being a flirt the secret of happiness?
explanation.walkthrough: Split differently, the answer reads A TEASE, a flirt; 'to be' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed and comfortable, as content people are, is the sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Nothing new in extremes of Sartre's language

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the outer letters of the philosopher's name
extremes of means the first and last letters of the name are used

parts.note: the name Sartre, with the possessive ending ignored
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Nothing original appears in the extreme parts of Sartre's writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' takes S and E from SARTRE (the possessive is ignored); 'in' puts LOVE and N between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Slavic tongue spoken in Slovenia is a national language of central Europe.

clue.text: Friendliness of retired toff, one in institution

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a nob is an upper-class person, a toff

indicators.note: in means the numeral sits inside the word for institution

parts.note: a home is a residential institution, such as a care home
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A posh old gentleman, now in a care home, is admired for his good nature.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is a British word for an upper-class person. 'retired' reverses NOB to give BON.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-natured geniality and cheerful warmth towards others is what friendliness amounts to.

clue.text: Contemptible chap in love with States

parts.note: he refers to a male, a chap
O is love, a zero score in tennis
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A despicable man is in love with America.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly wicked and shocking acts are odious and deserving of scorn.

clue.text: Escort impressed American, old record being brought up

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, impressed in the old sense of conscripted

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a log is a written record

explanation.surface: An American is wowed as an old record is mentioned again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressed' looks like 'awed', but it means press-ganged: a drafted US soldier. 'being brought up' reverses O LOG to give GOLO.
explanation.definitionFit: A man paid to accompany a wealthy woman is a hired male companion.

clue.text: Writer repeatedly dismissing hesitation in masterful manner

parts.note: an author is a writer

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the hesitation sound is removed from the word

parts.note: iteratively means repeatedly
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An assertive author keeps cutting out the ums and ers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' removes ER from ITERATIVELY, leaving ITATIVELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with confident command and expertise is how someone with commanding authority behaves.

clue.text: Area needing new leader to make a profit

indicators.note: needing a new leader means the first letter of the word is replaced with another

parts.note: a field is an area of land or of study

explanation.surface: A region needs a new boss to turn a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing new leader' swaps the F of FIELD for a different first letter, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Investments that produce returns earn money, so to give a return means to earn a gain.

clue.text: Spicy food pioneer cooked, keeping very quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the anagram wraps round the musical letters
cooked suggests the letters are altered or fiddled into a new order

parts.note: pp (pianissimo) is the musical instruction for very quiet

explanation.surface: A culinary innovator quietly makes something spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like it belongs with 'Spicy food', but it is the anagram signal for 'pioneer'; 'keeping' puts the musical sign for very quiet inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiced Italian dry sausage, often sliced as a pizza topping, is a hot cured meat.

clue.text: On reflection, fast talking is normal

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: rap is rhythmic fast talking over music

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a fast talker is just average.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' looks like 'having thought about it', but it reverses RAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up to standard or average is the idiomatic sense of being level with the expected score.

clue.text: Hold forth with enough people there, no question

indicators.note: no means without, so the question letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: a meeting is quorate when enough members are present to make decisions

explanation.surface: A speaker addresses a meeting that has a quorum, with no questions allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes QU from QUORATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak at length in a pompous, declaiming way is to deliver a speech.

clue.text: Dictator's sinister observation post?

indicators.note: a dictator here is one who dictates, speaking aloud, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: eerie means strange and sinister

explanation.surface: A tyrant keeps a menacing lookout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' looks like a tyrant but is someone speaking aloud. The definition is playful: an eagle's high nest looks down over everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's lofty nest on a crag looks out over the land, so it is jokingly a lookout.

clue.text: Budget problem proves Ned wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are put in an incorrect order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Ned's errors are shown up by a budget shortfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges PROVES NED.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending more than planned is the classic way a budget goes awry.
